summary: Scientific learning uses observation, test, experiment, research, survey, project work and model making.
Observation is experiencing an object, event or process carefully with the sense organs; a hand lens or microscope helps. It is the first step of any scientific study.
A hypothesis is a guess made from observation; a test checks whether it is true. In an experiment only one factor is changed.

Laboratory rules: apron/lab coat, gloves and goggles with harmful chemicals, no eating, drinking, tasting or direct smelling, no playing, test-tube holder for heating, fumes in a fume hood, wash hands after work.
Research steps: goal setting → hypothesis → choice of data-collection method → materials → data collection → analysis → conclusion.
Survey steps: objective → method → data collection → analysis → conclusion; tools are questionnaire, interview, discussion and observation.
Every activity ends with a report: title, objective, materials, method, observation/analysis, conclusion.
Every measurement needs a number and a unit; density = mass ÷ volume.

summary: ICT tools create, store, display, send and exchange information: ATM, photocopier, scanner (input, hard → soft copy), printer (output, soft → hard copy), router, Wi-Fi, set-top box.
ATM input parts: card reader, keypad; output parts: screen, speaker, receipt printer, cash dispenser. Keep the PIN secret.
A search engine finds web pages by keyword; a website is a collection of web pages with a unique URL; an ISP sells internet access.
Social media is a strong medium but overuse harms health and invites fake accounts, data leaks and phishing.
Cybercrime: identity theft, cyber terrorism, cyberbullying, hacking, defamation. Cyber law in Nepal: Electronic Transactions Act, 2063.
Internet security: strong passwords, two-factor authentication, updates, antivirus, firewall, backup, digital signatures.
Robotics designs robots; VR creates a 3-D artificial world; AI makes machines think; cloud computing stores and runs data on internet servers.

Full forms: ATM = Automated Teller Machine, WWW = World Wide Web, URL = Uniform Resource Locator, Wi-Fi = Wireless Fidelity, ISP = Internet Service Provider, VR = Virtual Reality, AI = Artificial Intelligence, STB = Set-Top Box.

Cell, tissue, organ and organ system in the human body
Classification of living beings
Effects of microorganisms
Protection of food from microorganisms; vaccination

summary: The cell is the structural and functional unit of life (Hooke, 1665).
Parts: covering (cell wall + membrane), cytoplasm, cell components (organelles + inclusions), nucleus.

Mitochondria = power house (ATP); chloroplast = photosynthesis; ribosome = protein factory; ER = endoskeleton; Golgi = secretion; lysosome = suicidal bag; nucleus = brain of the cell; human cells have 23 pairs of chromosomes.
Plant cells have a cell wall, plastids and a large vacuole; animal cells do not.
Cell → tissue → organ → organ system → body.
Two-kingdom system: Linnaeus, 1753. Five-kingdom system: Whittaker, 1969 — Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia.
Virus = link between living and non-living; bacteria, amoeba and fungi have useful and harmful effects.
Food preservation: dry, wet and cold methods remove moisture, add salt/acid/oil or lower the temperature. Vaccines give immunity.

summary: Biodiversity = variety of organisms; types: genetic, species and ecosystem diversity (Earth Summit, Rio de Janeiro, 1992).
Importance: food and livelihood, balanced environment, sustainable resources, ecotourism, adaptation to climate change.
Nepal: 0.1 % of world area, altitude 59 m – 8848.86 m, 3.2 % of plant and 1.1 % of animal species, 118 ecosystems; spiny babbler is endemic.
Degradation: overgrazing, pollution, mining, unplanned construction, deforestation, fire, floods, global warming, poaching, invasive species.
In-situ (national parks, reserves, conservation areas) and ex-situ (zoo, botanical garden, seed bank) conservation.
Food chains start with producers; joined food chains form a food web.
Sustainable development (Brundtland, 1987) has economic, social and environmental pillars, and principles of conservation, population control and public participation.
SDGs: 2016–2030, 17 goals, 169 targets, 232 indicators; goal 15 is about life on land and biodiversity.

summary: Reproduction gives birth to one's own kind; it is asexual (no gametes) or sexual (fusion of gametes).
Asexual types: fission, budding, fragmentation, regeneration, sporulation, parthenogenesis. Offspring are identical to the parent.
Vegetative propagation: natural (root, sucker, rhizome, corm, bulb, tuber, aerial stem, bulbil, leaf) and artificial (cutting, layering, gootee, grafting, tissue culture).
Flower: sepals, petals, stamens (anther + filament), pistil (stigma + style + ovary).
Pollination: self (autogamy, geitonogamy) and cross (wind, water, insects, birds).
Double fertilisation: male gamete + egg → zygote; male gamete + secondary nucleus → endosperm. Ovule → seed; ovary → fruit.
Animals: internal fertilisation (insects, reptiles, birds, mammals) and external (fish, frog).
Seed = seed coat + embryo (radicle, plumule, cotyledons) + endosperm; dispersed by wind, water, animals, gravity and bursting; germinates with water, air and warmth.

summary: Rest and motion are relative to a reference point. Speed =(d)/(t), velocity =(s)/(t) (m/s); velocity has direction.
Relative velocity: vA-vB (same direction), vA+vB (opposite).
Average velocity = total displacement ÷ total time =(u+v)/(2) for steady change.
Acceleration a=(v-u)/(t) (m/s²); negative acceleration is retardation.
Slope of d–t graph = speed; slope of v–t graph = acceleration; area under v–t = distance.
Newton: inertia; F=ma; action = reaction.
Lever: E× E.D.=L× L.D.; MA=(L)/(E), VR=(E.D.)/(L.D.), η=(MA)/(VR)×100% (< 100 % because of friction).
Pressure P=(F)/(A) (Pa); liquid pressure P=hdg; atmospheric pressure at sea level = 760 mmHg; barometer, manometer, pressure gauge.

summary: Energy is the capacity to do work (J); 1 calorie ≈ 4.2 J.
Heat flows from higher to lower temperature. F=(9)/(5)C+32, K=C+273.
Conduction (solids, no movement of particles), convection (liquids and gases, movement of particles), radiation (no medium, electromagnetic waves).
Dark surfaces absorb and emit radiation well; white and shiny surfaces do not.
Thermos flask: vacuum (no conduction/convection), silvering (no radiation), cork.
Greenhouse effect: greenhouse gases trap heat; more gases → global warming.
Q=msΔ t; water has a high specific heat capacity (4200 J/kg °C).
Concave mirror converges (real images, except object within F); convex mirror diverges (virtual, erect, diminished image). f=(R)/(2).

summary: Magnets attract iron, cobalt and nickel; like poles repel, unlike poles attract; a suspended magnet points north–south.
Natural magnet: lodestone. Artificial: bar, horseshoe, electromagnet.
Molecular theory (Weber, Ewing): aligned molecular magnets = magnet; random = unmagnetised; all aligned = saturation. Heating, hammering, a.c. and like-pole storage demagnetise.
Earth is a magnet (molten iron in the outer core). Declination: angle between geographic and magnetic meridians. Dip: angle with the horizontal (0° at magnetic equator, 90° at poles).
V=IR (Ohm's law); current in A, p.d. in V, resistance in Ω.
House supply 220 V: meter → main switch → distribution board (MCB/fuse) → switches → loads in parallel. Fuse and switch in the live wire; earth wire protects from shock.
1 unit = 1 kWh; E=P× N× t; bill = units × rate.

summary: Matter has mass and volume; it exists as solid, liquid and gas.
Atom: nucleus (protons +1, 1 amu; neutrons 0, 1 amu) and electrons (−1, 1/1837 amu) in shells K, L, M, N with at most 2n^2 electrons.
Valency = electrons lost, gained or shared to become stable; noble gases have valency 0.
Criss-cross method gives formulae (MgO, CaCl₂, AlCl₃, NH₃, K₂O).
Atomic weight = protons + neutrons; molecular weight = sum of atomic weights.
Chemical equation: reactants → products; balance by coefficients (2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl).
Modern periodic law (Moseley): properties depend on atomic number; 18 groups, 7 periods. Down a group size and metallic character increase; across a period they decrease.
pH < 7 acid, 7 neutral, > 7 base; acid + base → salt + water.

summary: Hard water has Ca and Mg salts. Temporary (bicarbonates): boiling, Clark's method. Permanent (sulphates, chlorides): washing soda, permutit.
Water is purified by sedimentation, filtration, boiling, chlorination, SODIS, distillation.
Acid rain: SO₂ and NOₓ from burning fuels form H₂SO₄ and HNO₃; harms water life, crops, forests and monuments.
Acid gives H⁺ (sour, blue litmus → red, methyl orange red, phenolphthalein colourless). Base/alkali gives OH⁻ (bitter, soapy, red litmus → blue, methyl orange yellow, phenolphthalein pink).
Acid + metal → salt + H₂; acid + carbonate → salt + H₂O + CO₂; acid + base → salt + water.
Salts are neutral (NaCl), acidic (NH₄Cl) or basic (Na₂CO₃).
Alloys: steel (Fe + C), stainless steel (Fe + Cr + Ni), brass (Cu + Zn), bronze (Cu + Sn).

summary: Mineral: natural, solid, homogeneous substance of definite composition; types — metallic (ferrous, non-ferrous, precious), non-metallic (gems, non-gems), energy minerals.
Nepal has more than 60 kinds of minerals; e.g. iron at Phulchoki, limestone at Udayapur, magnesite at Dolakha, uranium in Upper Mustang.
Earth's layers: crust, mantle, outer core (liquid), inner core (solid). Rocks: igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic.
Earth is about 4.6 billion years old. Hypotheses: nebular (Kant, Laplace), collision (Buffon), passing-star / planetesimal (Chamberlin–Moulton), tidal (Jeans–Jeffreys).
Eras: Cryptozoic (simple life), Palaeozoic (invertebrates, fish, amphibians, ferns), Mesozoic (reptiles, dinosaurs, conifers), Cenozoic (mammals, flowering plants, humans).
Big Bang: about 13.8 billion years ago; the universe is expanding (Hubble, Lemaître).
Asteroids: rocky, between Mars and Jupiter. Comets: icy, nucleus + coma + tails pointing away from the sun. Meteor = burning meteoroid; meteorite = piece that reaches the ground.
Galaxy: billions of stars (Milky Way); constellation: star pattern (88; 12 zodiac).
